cards.text: One of the seven angels with the seven bowls comes to John, the one seeing this vision (Revelation 1:9). The angel says, "Come, I will show you the punishment of the great prostitute, who sits on many waters." Friend, the last time an angel came to talk to me, I was flat on my back under a takeout menu.

cards.question: According to the angel, who was immoral with the great prostitute?
True or false: the angel says the people who dwell on the earth stayed clear of her immorality.

cards.text: Then the angel carries John away in the Spirit into a wilderness, and there's a woman sitting on a scarlet beast. No map, no directions, no "are we there yet."

cards.question: What is the scarlet beast covered with?
The scarlet beast the woman sits on has ___ heads and ___ horns.

cards.text: The woman is decked out in purple and scarlet, with gold, precious stones and pearls. I spent years in a drawer wearing DUST, friend, and she's wearing a whole jewelry store.

cards.question: What does the woman on the scarlet beast hold in her hand?

answers.text: a golden cup full of abominations
a golden bowl full of incense
a scroll sealed with seven seals

cards.text: Then John sees a mysterious name written right on her forehead. Not on a name tag, friend. On her FOREHEAD.

cards.question: What name is written on the woman's forehead?
True or false: the name on her forehead also calls her the mother of prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth.

cards.text: Then John can see that the woman is drunk, and it's not on wine.

cards.question: What is the woman on the scarlet beast drunk with?

answers.text: the blood of the saints and witnesses for Jesus
the riches of the kings of the whole earth
the praise of the many nations and peoples

cards.text: John has seen a LOT in this vision, and this sight leaves him utterly amazed. I bet his jaw is somewhere down by his sandals.

cards.question: The angel sees how amazed John is. What does the angel do next?

answers.text: tells him to close his eyes
tells him to write it down

cards.text: First, the beast. The angel says it was, and now is no more, but is about to come up out of the Abyss.

cards.question: After the beast comes up out of the Abyss, where does the angel say it goes?

cards.text: Then the angel talks about the people on earth whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world.

cards.question: When the people whose names aren't in the Book of Life see the beast, how do they react?

cards.text: The angel says, "This calls for a mind with wisdom." Friend, when an angel says that, you put the whisk DOWN and lean in.

cards.question: The angel starts with the beast's seven heads. What does he say they are?

answers.text: seven mountains where the woman sits
seven churches in the land of Asia

cards.text: Then the angel adds, "There are also seven kings. Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come."

cards.question: When the last of those seven kings does come, how long does the angel say he stays?
The angel says the beast that was, and now is not, is a king too. Which king?

cards.text: Next up, the beast's ten horns. The angel says they're ten kings who haven't received a kingdom yet.

cards.question: How long will those ten kings have authority as kings along with the beast?

cards.text: ONE HOUR. Friend, that's not a reign, that's a lunch break!

cards.question: The angel says these ten kings have one purpose. What is it?

answers.text: to yield their power to the beast
to make the woman their queen

cards.text: Then those ten kings take it a step further. They make war against the Lamb.

cards.question: Who triumphs in the war between the ten kings and the Lamb?
Why does the Lamb triumph over the ten kings?

answers.text: He is Lord of lords and King of kings
the ten kings turn on each other
the angels fight the battle for Him

cards.question: True or false: the Lamb goes into that war alone.

cards.text: His called and chosen and faithful ones are right there with Him. Friend, THAT is a guest list I'd bake for.

cards.question: The angel goes back to the many waters where the prostitute was sitting. What does he say those waters are?

answers.text: peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues
the seas and rivers of the whole earth
the tears of the saints and witnesses

cards.question: How does the angel say the ten horns and the beast will feel about the prostitute?

cards.text: They'll leave her desolate and naked, eat her flesh and burn her with fire. The very beast that carried her turns on her.

cards.question: The angel says someone put it into their hearts to unite and give their kingdom to the beast. Who?
Last thing the angel explains is the woman herself. What does he say she is?

answers.text: the great city that rules the kings of the earth
a queen from a land far beyond the sea
an idol the kings of the earth set up

cards.text: The woman is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth. And that's where we'll pause, friend, because this story is far from over.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "are we there yet.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Then John sees a mysterious name written right on her forehead." "Not on a name tag, friend." "On her FOREHEAD." A non-opening story card can have at most two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke "no 'are we there yet'" is the classic line of a child on a family car trip. It is a kid and parent scenario.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: "What is the scarlet beast covered with?" asks the baker to guess a descriptive detail of the vision (blasphemous names, eyes or breastplates). It does not ask about the movement or meaning. This matches the Psalm 23 bad example about what David's head is anointed with.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: "What does the woman on the scarlet beast hold in her hand?" asks the baker to guess a detail (cup, bowl or scroll) with no setup to reason from. This matches the Psalm 23 bad example ("guessing a detail: oil, myrrh or perfume?").

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: Most choice cards in stop 1 can only be answered by luck, because the story card before them gives nothing to reason from. These are cards 2 (who was immoral with her), 5 (what the beast is covered with), 6 (number of heads and horns), 8 (what she holds) and 10 (the name on her forehead, after a card that only says "a mysterious name"). That is more than a few discovery questions, so informed guesses are not the majority.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1: 8 of the 11 choice cards are multiple choice, against 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2 by a wide margin: 11 of the 12 choice cards are multiple choice, with one true or false and no fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card ("ONE HOUR. Friend, that's not a reign, that's a lunch break!") only reacts to the answer of card 7. It tells no new part of the passage, so it doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The last story card repeats the answer of card 19 ("The woman is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.") before the line saying the story continues. That is a recap. Because 17:18 was already asked on a choice card, the card can be just the line saying the story isn't over.
The Lamb first shows up in this passage on this card, but no card says simply who the Lamb is (Jesus, with a reference such as John 1:29).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer, "He is Lord of lords and King of kings", is a well-known biblical title. The wrong answers are plain descriptions of events ("the ten kings turn on each other", "the angels fight the battle for Him"). The answers are not the same kind of thing, and the right one sounds more like the Bible.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Revelation 17:17 says God put it into their hearts "to carry out His purpose", and that this lasts "until the words of God are fulfilled." No card tells either part. The card reduces the verse to uniting to give their kingdom to the beast, so the baker misses that God's purpose and His words are behind it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
